correctness.rationale: The Ye–Wu–Liu–Yu blow-up theorem gives six independent classes with weights lambda_i and lambda_i lambda_j and quotient B3. False twins force every zero forcing set to leave at most one vertex per class. Relabeling so lambda_3>1 gives permanently blue representatives in C3,L1,L2; an explicit forcing sequence clears C1,C2, then C3/L3 even when lambda_1=lambda_2=1, and finally the remaining leaves. Thus all and only the at-most-one-white-per-class profiles force, giving the product polynomial and minimum-set count. The B3 adjacency matrix has determinant -1, so its independent-set blow-up has rank six. Since Z=N-6 and M<=Z, minimum rank is exactly six. The six root magnitudes are {lambda_i,lambda_i lambda_j}; their two smallest values are the two smallest lambda_i and their total product is (lambda_1 lambda_2 lambda_3)^3, proving exact recovery.

value.rationale: The theorem establishes a complete graph invariant on a natural three-local algebraic class and gives a closed inverse map from polynomial roots to local ideal counts. For chain-ring factors those recovered integers are precisely the nilpotency lengths, so the graph polynomial carries concrete algebraic structure. The result also supplies exact maximum nullity, real minimum rank, and every minimum forcing set, making it substantially more informative than a routine type-profile evaluation.
